successCriteria.description: `LeavePolicyRepository.findByLeaveType` filters by `is_active = true` in its SQL query, so it only returns the active policy for a given LeaveType (or null if none is active), enforcing the invariant "Each LeaveType has exactly one active LeavePolicy at any time."
`EmployeeService.isActive` uses the `EmploymentStatus.ACTIVE` enum value (not the string literal `'ACTIVE'`) when comparing `employee.employmentStatus`.

The `leave-policy.service.spec.ts` test "should return false when policy exists but is inactive" is updated: `findByLeaveType` now returns null for an inactive policy (since the repository filters to active-only), and `isLeaveTypeActive` correctly returns false when no active policy is found.

`ARCHITECTURE.md` is updated so the `leave-policy` module description accurately states that `findByLeaveType` returns only the active policy for a given LeaveType (or null), consistent with the invariant "Each LeaveType has exactly one active LeavePolicy at any time."

constraints: No new modules, files, or exports may be introduced — this phase only modifies existing files: `src/modules/leave-policy/leave-policy.repository.ts`, `src/modules/employee/employee.service.ts`, `tests/unit/modules/leave-policy/leave-policy.service.spec.ts`, and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

The `ILeavePolicyRepository` interface signature for `findByLeaveType` must not change — it still accepts `LeaveType` and optional `PoolClient` and returns `Promise<LeavePolicy | null>`. Only the SQL implementation changes.

The `IEmployeeService` interface signature for `isActive` must not change — it still accepts `id: string` and returns `Promise<boolean>`. Only the implementation's comparison changes from string literal to enum.

All existing tests in `employee.service.spec.ts` must continue to pass without modification. All existing tests in `leave-policy.service.spec.ts` must pass after the one test case is updated; no other test cases may be removed or altered.

ambiguities.description: After fixing `findByLeaveType` to return only active policies, the `isLeaveTypeActive` method's `policy.isActive` check becomes redundant (it will always be true when policy is non-null). Should the service method be simplified to `return policy !== null`, or should the redundant check remain as a defensive guard?
options: Simplify to `return policy !== null` — the repository now guarantees active-only results
Keep the `policy.isActive` check as a defensive guard — harmless redundancy

entityInvariants.invariant: For any given LeaveType, at most one LeavePolicy with `isActive = true` exists at any time. The `findByLeaveType` repository method MUST enforce this by filtering `is_active = true` in its query, returning the single active policy or null.

The `employmentStatus` field is typed as the `EmploymentStatus` enum. All comparisons against this field MUST use the enum values (`EmploymentStatus.ACTIVE`, `EmploymentStatus.INACTIVE`, `EmploymentStatus.TERMINATED`), never raw string literals.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the single active LeavePolicy for the given LeaveType, or null if no active policy exists. Must not return inactive policies.
Throws NotFoundError if employee does not exist. Returns boolean: true only when employmentStatus equals EmploymentStatus.ACTIVE.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The `findByLeaveType` SQL query must match the reconciled architecture invariant: "Each LeaveType has exactly one active LeavePolicy at any time." The query must include `AND is_active = true`.
The `isActive` method must use the `EmploymentStatus` enum from `shared/types` for its comparison, matching the type declared in `employee.model.ts`.
consistencyRequirements.referencePath: src/modules/employee/employee.model.ts → employmentStatus field typed as EmploymentStatus
